info.name: ATW Backend — Masterdata
info.description:
# ATW Backend — Masterdata

Reference/lookup data shared across the whole platform: internal org departments, the industry -> designation -> skill hierarchy vacancies will be posted under, skill-category groupings used purely for minimum-wage lookups, and state/city geography for address dropdowns. Legacy PHP had this as ad-hoc, under-validated tables (no RBAC on department at all, a `cities` table that was actually district-grain with only ~590 of ~750+ real districts) - this module rebuilds it with full CRUD, RBAC, and properly seeded reference data.

**Run order:** Geography is seeded, read-only reference data - run its two requests first just to capture `{{stateId}}`/`{{cityId}}` for later use. Then Departments / Industries / Skill Categories (independent of each other and of everything else) -> Designations (needs an `industryId`, optionally a `skillCategoryId`) -> Skills (needs a `designationId`) -> Minimum Wage Rates (needs a `stateId` + `skillCategoryId`). Each resource folder's **Delete**/**Bulk Delete** requests are placed last within that folder and are genuinely destructive against the `{{xId}}` variable earlier requests in the same folder saved - if you run a whole folder top-to-bottom (or the whole collection via Collection Runner), re-run that folder's **Create** request before continuing to a folder that depends on its id (e.g. re-run Create Industry before Create Designation if Delete Industry already ran in the same pass).

**Shared conventions across every admin resource in this folder:**
- `status` is always the same 2-value enum, `"ACTIVE"` / `"INACTIVE"`.
- Every `GET /` list endpoint now returns a paginated `PageResponse` (`{content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages, first, last}`) - default page size 100, max 500 (`spring.data.web.pageable.default-page-size` / `.max-page-size` in `application.properties`); standard `?page=&size=&sort=` apply. Minimum Wage Rates was always paginated this way - every other entity in this folder was upgraded to match it this session (previously an unpaginated plain array).
- Every list endpoint accepts multiselect filters as **repeated** query params (e.g. `?statuses=ACTIVE&statuses=INACTIVE`), not a single value, plus free-text `?search=` (case-insensitive substring match on `name`) where the entity has one. Sorting by an unsupported `sort` property returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before the query ever runs - see each folder's List request for its own filters and allowed sort fields.
- `DELETE .../{id}` and `POST .../bulk-delete` now exist for every entity in this folder **except Minimum Wage Rates** (an append-only statutory history - see that folder's description for why) - a real, hard delete guarded by the relevant foreign-key constraint, returning a friendly `409 CONFLICT` (not a raw database error) when the row is still referenced elsewhere. The status-toggle endpoints remain available for a non-destructive deactivation instead.
- `POST .../bulk-status` (every entity) and `POST .../bulk-delete` (every entity except Minimum Wage Rates) both take a batch of ids and process each independently - partial success is normal; check the response's `failures` array for any id that was skipped and why.
- `POST .../{id}/status` always takes an explicit `{status: "ACTIVE"|"INACTIVE"}` target rather than blindly toggling - same reasoning as the existing Staff status endpoint: two quick calls can't race each other into an unpredictable end state the way a blind toggle could.
- Icon uploads (Industries/Designations/Skills only - Departments and Skill Categories have no image) are always a separate `PUT .../{id}/image` / `DELETE .../{id}/image` pair, never a field on the main create/update body - see the Industries folder description for why.

For admin login/2FA, see **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json**; for staff/role administration,
see **ATW-RBAC-Staff.postman_collection.json**.

Every endpoint is versioned under `/api/v1/` and returns the same envelope:

```
{ "success": boolean, "data": <payload> | null, "error": <ApiError> | null }
```

`ApiError` shape: `{"code": string, "message": string, "fieldErrors": [{"field","message"}] | null, "timestamp": ISO-8601 string, "traceId": string | null}`. `fieldErrors` is populated only for `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses that came from `@Valid` request-body validation; it's `null`/omitted for every other error, including other `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses raised programmatically (e.g. "Unknown permission code(s)"). `traceId` echoes the `X-Correlation-Id` request header when present — include it when reporting a bug.

## Running this collection

Select the **ATW Backend - Local** environment first, and run **Login** / **Verify OTP** from the
Auth & Account collection to populate `{{accessToken}}` — every request here requires it (the two
Geography lookups need just a valid token; everything else additionally needs its own `<module>.*`
permission). Folders roughly mirror dependency order:

1. **Geography** is seed data (36 states, 784 districts) — read-only, nothing to create here.
2. **Departments**, **Industries**, **Skill Categories** have no dependencies on each other — create
   any of them first.
3. **Designations** depends on at least one **Industry** existing (`industryIds[]` requires ≥1) and
   optionally a **Skill Category**; its own Create/Update/status/image requests save
   `{{designationId}}` and reference `{{industryId}}` / `{{skillCategoryId}}`.
4. **Skills** depends on a **Designation** existing (`designationId` is required); save
   `{{skillId}}`.
5. **Minimum Wage Rates** depends on a **State** (from Geography) and a **Skill Category** existing;
   it's effective-dated and immutable — there is no edit endpoint, only create-a-new-version and
   activate/deactivate.
6. **Delete** and **Bulk Delete** (every resource except Minimum Wage Rates) are destructive and are
   placed as the last requests in each folder for that reason. They're guarded by the same foreign
   keys the underlying tables already had (worker/designation/skill references) and come back as a
   friendly `409 CONFLICT` — never a raw database error — when the row is still referenced elsewhere;
   see each folder's own Delete request for its exact conflict message. Running one consumes the id
   that folder's Create request saved, so re-run Create first if you need that id again afterward.

## Error codes that can appear on (almost) any endpoint

These are produced centrally — by `GlobalExceptionHandler`, by Spring Security's entry point / access-denied handler, or by the two security filters that run before a controller is even reached — so they are **not** re-documented on every individual request below; only an endpoint's *specific* codes and triggers are. Two pairs are easy to confuse and worth reading carefully:

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | A `@Valid` request-body field failed Bean Validation (`fieldErrors[]` present), or a service-level input check failed (no `fieldErrors`). |
| `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | 400 | Request body is missing or isn't valid JSON. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | `Content-Type` isn't `application/json`. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | **No bearer token was presented at all**, or it's malformed/expired/signature-invalid. Produced by Spring Security itself, before any controller runs. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | A **business-level** auth failure on an endpoint that doesn't require a token in the first place — bad login credentials, a locked/disabled account, an invalid refresh/reset/invite token. Same HTTP status as `UNAUTHENTICATED` above, different meaning: this means "the token/credential you supplied is bad", not "you supplied nothing". |
| `SESSION_REVOKED` | 401 | The bearer token parses fine, but the admin's `security_version` has moved on since it was issued (password changed/reset, or their role assignment changed), or the account is no longer `ACTIVE`. The client must discard tokens and log in again — refreshing won't help, the refresh token was revoked too. |
| `MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD` | 403 | Authenticated, but the token's `mustChangePassword` flag is set and this isn't `/admin/account/me` or `/admin/account/change-password`. |
| `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 | Authenticated, but lacking the specific permission the endpoint requires. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests to one of the 6 public, abuse-prone auth endpoints from the same IP within the window — default 10 requests/60s, **per endpoint**, not pooled across them. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The **URL itself** doesn't match any endpoint (a routing miss — typo'd path, wrong version prefix, etc). |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The URL is valid, but the specific id in it (a staff id, role id, ...) doesn't exist. Different from `NOT_FOUND` above — don't conflate "no such route" with "no such record". |
| `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | 405 | Right URL, wrong HTTP verb. |
| `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | Input is syntactically well-formed but violates a business rule (e.g. "system roles cannot be modified", a privilege-escalation attempt, self/super-admin protection). |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | Either an endpoint's own duplicate check (most common — a friendlier, specific message), or a generic last-resort safety net when a unique-constraint violation reaches the database despite an earlier application-level check passing (a genuine race between two concurrent requests) — that fallback case always carries the same generic message, regardless of which field collided. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Full detail (stack trace) is logged server-side against the same `traceId` returned to the client; never returned in the response body itself. |

## Documentation cross-references

- **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json** — login/2FA and a caller's own account self-service.
- **ATW-RBAC-Staff.postman_collection.json** — role/permission management and staff administration.
- **ATW-Health.postman_collection.json** — unauthenticated liveness/readiness checks; useful to rule
  out "`{{baseUrl}}` unreachable" before chasing what looks like an `UNAUTHENTICATED` response.
- `FRONTEND_HANDOVER.md` §4 "Masterdata" — the full endpoint reference in table form.
- `HANDOVER.md` — Azure deployment context, including the V17–V21 migrations that introduced this
  module.

Worker-side modules that reference this module's lookup data (a worker's `departmentId`, and their
industry/designation/skill selections) are documented in their own collections, authored alongside
this one: `ATW-Worker.postman_collection.json`, `ATW-Worker-KYC.postman_collection.json` and
`ATW-Worker-FaceAuth.postman_collection.json` (named here for reference - not linked, since they're
written concurrently with this file).

item.name: Geography
item.description:
Public read-only dropdowns for address forms, under `/api/v1/masterdata/**` (not nested under `/admin` - this data is identical for every actor, admin today and company/worker once those sides exist). Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` (the application-wide default) but **no specific permission** - it's non-sensitive reference data. 36 Indian states/UTs and 784 districts, both seeded via Flyway migration and never created through this API.

**Terminology note:** this data is at district grain (e.g. Jaipur, Jodhpur, and Udaipur are all separate entries under Rajasthan), but ATW's own product vocabulary deliberately calls it "city" rather than "district" throughout the API - a product/UX decision, not a data-modeling one.

request.description:
**Permission:** none beyond authentication.

Returns all 36 Indian states/UTs as `StateSummary[]` = `{id, name, code}` (ISO 3166-2:IN subdivision codes, e.g. `IN-RJ` for Rajasthan), sorted by name. Fixed reference data seeded by Flyway - there is no create/update/delete for states through this API.

This request's Tests script saves the first result's id to `{{stateId}}` for the requests below that need one.

**Permission:** none beyond authentication.

Returns every district (ATW's API calls it "city" - see the folder description) under the given state as `CitySummary[]` = `{id, name}`, sorted by name.

**Behavior:** an unknown or nonexistent `stateId` is **not** an error - it returns an empty array `[]`, exactly as it would for a real state that happens to have zero seeded cities. There is no existence check on `stateId` for this read (confirmed against `GeographyLookupServiceImpl` - contrast with every **write** endpoint elsewhere in this module, which does validate foreign ids and returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` for an unknown one). This is intentional: a dropdown's "no results" state and "bad id" state render identically to the end user, so an extra existence-check query would cost something for no behavioral benefit.

This request's Tests script saves the first result's id to `{{cityId}}` for the requests below that need one.

response.name: 200 - Unknown stateId returns an empty array, not a 404

item.name: Departments
item.description: ATW's own internal org structure - which team an admin staff member (or, later, an agent) belongs to. Entirely unrelated to the industry/designation/skill hierarchy below; don't confuse "department" (ATW's internal org chart) with "industry" (the external sector a vacancy belongs to). No icon support. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the matching `department.*` permission. Legacy had zero RBAC and no edit/delete at all for this table - that was a gap, not a deliberate design, so it gets the same full CRUD treatment as every other resource here.

query.description: Repeat for multiple values, e.g. ?statuses=ACTIVE&statuses=INACTIVE. Omit for every status.

request.description:
**Permission:** `department.view`.

Paginated, multiselect-filterable, free-text-searchable, sortable list of departments (active and inactive) as `PageResponse<DepartmentResponse>` = `{content: DepartmentResponse[], page, size, totalElements, totalPages, first, last}`, where `DepartmentResponse` = `{id, name, status}`.

**Query params (all optional)**
- `statuses` - repeat the param for multiple values, e.g. `?statuses=ACTIVE&statuses=INACTIVE`. Omit entirely for every status.
- `search` - case-insensitive substring match against `name`, as shown here.
- `page` / `size` - 0-based page index / page size. Default size is 100, max 500 (`spring.data.web.pageable.default-page-size` / `.max-page-size`).
- `sort` - defaults to `name,asc` when omitted. Allowed values: `name`, `status`, `createdAt` (e.g. `?sort=createdAt,desc`).

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unsupported `sort` property | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 400 - Unsupported sort property

request.description:
**Permission:** `department.view`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown department id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `department.create`.

**Validation**
- `name` - required, non-blank, max 150 chars.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| A department with this name already exists | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{departmentId}}`.

response.name: 409 - Duplicate name

request.description:
**Permission:** `department.edit`.

Same validation and duplicate-name check as Create (excluding this department's own current row).

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown department id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Another department already has this name | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

**Permission:** `department.toggle_status`.

Takes an explicit target status rather than blindly toggling - see the folder description. There is no DELETE endpoint for departments - this status endpoint is the only way to retire one.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown department id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `department.toggle_status`.

Sets the same explicit target `status` on a batch of departments in one call. Each id is processed independently - partial success is normal and expected; check `data.failures` for any id that was skipped and why (currently only `"Not found"` for an unknown id, since a status change never hits a unique/FK constraint).

**Validation**
- `ids` - required, must not be empty.
- `status` - required.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` was empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 400 - ids was empty

request.description:
**Permission:** `department.delete`.

A real, hard delete - not a status flip. Guarded by the existing `worker.department_id REFERENCES department(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` foreign key: deleting a department that still has one or more workers assigned to it is rejected with a friendly 409, not a raw database error. Reassign those workers (or deactivate the department instead via **Set Department Status**) before retrying the delete.

This is placed last in this folder on purpose - it consumes `{{departmentId}}`. Re-run **Create Department** first if you need that variable again afterward.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown department id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Still referenced by one or more workers | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

response.name: 409 - Still referenced by workers

request.description:
**Permission:** `department.delete`.

Same FK guard as **Delete Department** above, applied per id. Deliberately NOT one shared transaction for the whole batch - each id commits or fails independently, so a conflict on one id can never roll back a sibling id's otherwise-successful delete. Check `data.failures` for which ids (if any) were skipped and why (`"Not found"` or the same friendly FK-conflict message as the single delete).

**Validation**
- `ids` - required, must not be empty.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` was empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 400 - ids was empty

item.name: Industries
item.description:
The external sector a vacancy belongs to (e.g. Construction, Manufacturing, Hospitality) - the top of the industry -> designation -> skill chain vacancies will be posted under. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the matching `industry.*` permission.

**`code` is backend-generated, not client-supplied:** format `IND` + a 7-digit sequence (e.g. `IND0000001`), assigned from a dedicated Postgres sequence the moment a row is created. There is no `code` field on Create or Update - it never changes after creation, and the old legacy-style "duplicate code" 409 no longer exists, since the client can't supply a colliding value in the first place.

**Icon uploads - read this once, it applies identically to Designations and Skills below too:**
- A separate `PUT .../{id}/image` (multipart, field name `file`) / `DELETE .../{id}/image` pair, never a field on the create/update body - this is deliberate: folding image data into the general update DTO would let a caller reference an arbitrary pre-existing document id (e.g. someone else's KYC scan) instead of actually uploading a new file.
- Allowed content types: **`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp` only** - `image/svg+xml` is deliberately excluded even though it's technically an image format, because an SVG can embed `<script>` and would be stored and re-served byte-for-byte by the underlying blob storage (no sniffing of its own) - opening the image URL directly in a browser could then execute attacker script in ATW's own origin. This is a real, deliberate security exclusion, not an oversight.
- Max size **2MB** - an icon, not a document scan (contrast with the Document module's general-purpose limits, which allow PDFs up to 10MB for KYC-grade uploads).
- The declared `Content-Type` is cross-checked against the file's actual leading bytes (PNG/JPEG magic numbers, or the WEBP RIFF container's own FourCC) - a mismatch is rejected with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, not silently trusted. All of this has dedicated unit tests exercising each rejection path.
- Uploading a new image when one already exists **replaces** it - the old blob is deleted.
- The returned `imageUrl` is a short-lived (~15 minute) signed URL - re-fetch the resource to get a fresh one rather than caching it; don't persist it client-side.
- **Performance note:** list endpoints (`GET /` with no id) never resolve `imageUrl` - it comes back `null` even for a row that has an icon. Resolving it requires a DB lookup plus a live signed-URL call per row, which is fine for a single `GET /{id}` but would make an unbounded list endpoint slower as more rows gain icons. Call `GET /{id}` when you actually need the image URL for a specific row.

query.description: Repeat for multiple values, e.g. ?statuses=ACTIVE&statuses=INACTIVE. Omit for every status.

request.description:
**Permission:** `industry.view`.

Paginated, multiselect-filterable, free-text-searchable, sortable list as `PageResponse<IndustryResponse>`, where `IndustryResponse` = `{id, name, code, status, imageUrl}`. `imageUrl` is always `null` here regardless of whether an icon was uploaded - see the folder description's performance note; call Get Industry for the real value.

**Query params (all optional)**
- `statuses` - multiselect.
- `search` - case-insensitive substring match against `name`.
- `page` / `size` - default size 100, max 500.
- `sort` - defaults to `name,asc`. Allowed values: `name`, `status`, `createdAt`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unsupported `sort` property | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Unsupported sort property

request.description:
**Permission:** `industry.view`.

Unlike List, this resolves a real `imageUrl` (a fresh ~15 minute signed URL) when an icon exists.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown industry id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `industry.create`.

**Validation**
- `name` - required, non-blank, max 150 chars.

There is no `code` field in the request body - `code` is generated server-side (a dedicated Postgres sequence, format `IND` + 7 digits, e.g. `IND0000001`) and returned in the response. It is never reused and never accepted from the client; if you send a `code` field anyway it is silently ignored (Spring Boot's default Jackson config does not fail on unknown JSON properties) rather than causing an error - don't rely on that, just omit the field.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| An industry with this name already exists | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{industryId}}`.

response.name: 409 - Duplicate name
response._comment: code is never client-supplied (see this folder's description), so the only remaining Create conflict is on name - unlike the old legacy-style API, there is no second 'duplicate code' scenario to hit.

request.description:
**Permission:** `industry.edit`.

Same `name` validation and duplicate-name check as Create (excluding this industry's own current row). There is no `code` field in this body either - it was assigned once at creation and is immutable thereafter.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown industry id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Another industry already has this name | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

**Permission:** `industry.toggle_status`.

Explicit target status, not a blind toggle - see the Masterdata folder description.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown industry id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `industry.toggle_status`.

Partial success is normal - each id is processed independently; check `data.failures` for any id that was skipped and why.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` was empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 400 - ids was empty

request.description:
**Permission:** `industry.edit`.

Multipart form-data with a single part, field name **`file`**. See the folder description for the full validation/security rationale (allow-list, magic-byte verification, 2MB cap, replace-deletes-old). Summary of checks, in order:

1. File must be non-empty.
2. File must be â‰¤2MB.
3. Declared `Content-Type` must be exactly `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, or `image/webp`.
4. The file's actual leading bytes must match that declared type (magic-byte check).

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| File is empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| File exceeds 2MB (also enforced earlier, at the multipart-parsing layer) | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| Content-Type isn't png/jpeg/webp | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 - message lists the 3 allowed types |
| Content-Type is allowed but the file's bytes don't actually match it | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 - "File content does not match declared content type X" |
| The file part has no Content-Type at all | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 (handled explicitly - this does **not** 500) |
| Unknown industry id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

response.name: 400 - File content does not match declared content type
response._comment: Triggered by, e.g., a .pdf or .txt file renamed to look like a .png and declared as image/png - the magic-byte check catches it even though the Content-Type header looks fine.

request.description:
**Permission:** `industry.edit`.

Clears the icon, if any. **Not an error if there was no image to begin with** - this is a "make sure there's no image" operation, not a "delete this specific image" one.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown industry id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `industry.delete`.

A real, hard delete. Guarded by the existing foreign keys from workers and designations into this table (`ON DELETE RESTRICT`) - deleting an industry that is still assigned to one or more workers or designations is rejected with a friendly 409, not a raw database error. Reassign those first, or deactivate the industry instead via **Set Industry Status**.

This is placed last in this folder on purpose - it consumes `{{industryId}}`, which the **Designations** folder below also depends on. Re-run **Create Industry** before running Designations' requests if this already ran in the same pass.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown industry id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Still assigned to one or more workers or designations | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

response.name: 409 - Still assigned to workers or designations

request.description:
**Permission:** `industry.delete`. Same FK guard as **Delete Industry** above, applied per id in its own transaction; check `data.failures` for any id that was skipped and why.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` was empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 400 - ids was empty

item.name: Skill Categories
item.description:
Purely a minimum-wage grouping (e.g. "Skilled", "Semi-Skilled", "Unskilled") - **not** part of the industry/designation/skill chain itself. The only connection is one optional field on a Designation (`skillCategoryId`), which is what lets Minimum Wage Rates below resolve a rate for a given designation indirectly. No icon support. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the matching `skill_category.*` permission.

**`code` is backend-generated, not client-supplied:** format `SKC` + a 7-digit sequence (e.g. `SKC0000001`), assigned from a dedicated Postgres sequence the moment a row is created. There is no `code` field on Create or Update, and it never changes afterward - the old legacy-style "duplicate code" 409 no longer applies, since the client can't supply a colliding value in the first place.

query.description: Repeat for multiple values, e.g. ?statuses=ACTIVE&statuses=INACTIVE. Omit for every status.

request.description:
**Permission:** `skill_category.view`.

Paginated, multiselect-filterable, free-text-searchable, sortable list as `PageResponse<SkillCategoryResponse>`, where `SkillCategoryResponse` = `{id, name, code, status}`. Default page size 100, max 500.

**Query params (all optional)**
- `statuses` - multiselect.
- `search` - case-insensitive substring match against `name`.
- `page` / `size`.
- `sort` - defaults to `name,asc`. Allowed values: `name`, `status`, `createdAt`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unsupported `sort` property | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 400 - Unsupported sort property

request.description:
**Permission:** `skill_category.view`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown skill category id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

**Permission:** `skill_category.create`.

**Validation**
- `name` - required, non-blank, max 150 chars.

There is no `code` field in the request body - `code` is generated server-side (a dedicated Postgres sequence, format `SKC` + 7 digits, e.g. `SKC0000001`) and returned in the response; it is never reused and never accepted from the client.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| A skill category with this name already exists | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{skillCategoryId}}`.

response.name: 409 - Duplicate name

request.description:
**Permission:** `skill_category.edit`.

Same `name` validation and duplicate-name check as Create (excluding this row's own current values). There is no `code` field here either - it was assigned once at creation and is immutable thereafter.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown skill category id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |

item.name: Minimum Wage Rates
item.description:
The statutory minimum daily wage for a (state, skill category) pair. **This is the one genuinely unusual resource in the whole Masterdata module - read this carefully before integrating.**

**Effective-dated and immutable:** a rate change is *always* a brand-new row with its own `effectiveFrom` date - never an edit of an existing row's rate, date, state, or category. There is **no PUT/edit endpoint for the rate value at all** - only Create (= a new version), a status toggle, and reads. This mirrors how real government minimum-wage notifications actually work (always dated, never retroactively rewritten) and preserves the full history needed to correctly recompute what rate legally applied during any past pay period - which payroll will eventually depend on.

**The only resource in this module with no Delete/Bulk Delete at all** (every other entity in this module now has both, guarded by foreign keys - see their own folders) - unlike those small, bounded, real-world lists (Department/Industry/Designation/Skill/Skill Category), this table is append-only statutory history; deleting a row would defeat the exact "reconstruct what rate legally applied on any past date" purpose it exists for. A mis-entered row is retracted via **Set Minimum Wage Rate Status** -> `INACTIVE` instead, never removed. `minimum_wage.edit`/`.delete` exist in the permission catalog (inherited from the legacy permission list) but are deliberately unused - there is no edit-the-value or delete endpoint for this entity at all.

**Also the only resource in this module that's paginated** (`GET /` returns a `PageResponse`, not a plain array) - it's the one table here that grows without bound over the years (append-only, immutable rows), unlike Department/Industry/Designation/Skill/Skill Category, which are small, bounded, real-world lists.

`MinimumWageRateResponse` = `{id, stateId, stateName, skillCategoryId, skillCategoryName, minDailyRate, effectiveFrom, status}` - the one DTO in this module that denormalizes human-readable names alongside the raw ids, purely for admin-grid display convenience.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` and the matching `minimum_wage.*` permission.

**Query params (all optional)**
- `stateIds` - multiselect, repeat the param for multiple states (`?stateIds=...&stateIds=...`). Note the plural: this is a **breaking rename** from the singular `stateId` this endpoint used before this session's listing-API enhancement - the singular form is no longer recognized.
- `skillCategoryIds` - multiselect, same repeated-param convention.

- `page` / `size` - default size 100, max 500.
- `sort` - defaults to `effectiveFrom,desc` (newest version first) when omitted. Allowed values: `effectiveFrom`, `minDailyRate`, `status`, `createdAt`.

**Permission:** `minimum_wage.view`.

Fetches one specific version by its own id - contrast with Resolve Effective Rate below, which looks up by state/category/date instead of a known row id.

|---|---|---|

**Permission:** `minimum_wage.view`.

The single most useful endpoint in this folder for other modules (future payroll/vacancy integrations): given a state + skill category, resolves whichever version was/is **actually in force** on a given date - the latest `ACTIVE` row whose `effectiveFrom` is on or before `asOf`.

**`asOf` is optional** - an ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); omit it to resolve "as of today" (in IST, not UTC - the server's clock is pinned to `Asia/Kolkata` specifically so this resolves correctly even in the early-morning UTC hours of an India calendar day). The example here deliberately asks about a **past** date, to show this endpoint can answer "what rate applied back then," not just "what's the current rate."

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| No rate configured for this state/category as of `asOf` (e.g. a date before any version ever existed) | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 - see the example below |

response.name: 200 - OK (resolves the version in force on that past date)
response._comment: asOf=2026-03-01 falls between the 2026-01-01 version (400.00) and the later 2026-07-01 version (450.00), so the OLDER version is correctly returned - this is a historical lookup, not just 'give me the latest row'.

response._comment: 2024-01-01 is before the earliest version (2026-01-01) was ever entered - there's genuinely no answer to 'what rate applied then', so this is a real 404, not a bug.

request.description:
**Permission:** `minimum_wage.create`.

**Always creates a new, independent version - there is no request shape for editing an existing rate's value.** See the folder description for why.

**Validation**
- `stateId` - required, must reference an existing state.
- `skillCategoryId` - required, must reference an existing skill category.
- `minDailyRate` - required, decimal > 0, up to 8 integer digits and exactly 2 fraction digits (e.g. `450.00`).
- `effectiveFrom` - required, ISO date.

**Errors** (checked in this order)

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `stateId` doesn't exist | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| `skillCategoryId` doesn't exist | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| An **ACTIVE** rate already exists for this exact (state, skill category, effectiveFrom) triple | `CONFLICT` | 409 - see the example below |

**On the 409:** a *deactivated* row's date can be reused - uniqueness only applies among `ACTIVE` rows. That's what makes correcting a mis-entered rate possible without losing the historical record that a mistake was made: deactivate the wrong row first (Set Minimum Wage Rate Status below), then create the real version with the same `effectiveFrom`.

This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{minimumWageRateId}}`.

response.name: 409 - An active version for this date already exists
response._comment: Same (state, skillCategory, effectiveFrom) as the version created above, regardless of the minDailyRate value sent - the conflict is on the triple, not the rate amount.
